title: Another normal week in 2023: death threats, censorship, cuts and investment
author: Ian Anstice / The Library Campaign

editorial.text: Advertisement Censoring libraries is hitting stronger all the time – this week we have (1) death threats against US and Irish libraries (2) Devon apparently (the papers reporting it are the Telegraph and Express so it’s not certain) restricting access to Enid Blyton (3) the Mail stoking outrage at a LGBT books in a British school library and a Michigan prosecutor considering an up-to-four-year jail term for a librarian for stocking a book he doesn’t agree with. It’s all pretty sickening. In other news, some New Zealand politician has come up with the brilliant idea of having volunteer libraries, Scotland is celebrating having a majority of fines-free libraries while at the same time fighting closures in Aberdeen, Cardiff still cutting jobs but by stealth, Hackney’s staff cuts completely accidently wiping out union stewards, Stockport getting a nice new co-located library, Stoke selling off libraries (including one that promptly caught on fire) and a potentially dodgy consultation In Worcestershire. Another normal week in 2023.
